newsitem.title: USA: CFTC display's assets to be auctioned on Internet.
newsitem.headline: CFTC display's assets to be auctioned on Internet.

text.p: Commodities regulators have found a new way of using their Internet site: displaying the property, which is to be auctioned on Saturday, of a missing man who has been accused of embezzling.
That's what the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the futures market regulator, did in a bid to show the assets of Donald Chancey for those who failed to see a pre-auction open house last week.
Chancey disappeared in May after the CFTC charged him with fraud for enticing people to invest in an unregistered commodity pool called Southeastern Venture Partners Group.
He allegedly embezzled $3 million, miusing investors money to pay for his personal and unrelated business expenses.
The CFTC said the World Wide Web pages it opened on its Internet site, www.cftc.gov, has photographs of Chancey's belongings, including oriental rugs, computer equipment, furniture and appliances.

The auction will be conducted at Chancey's house in Valdosta, Ga., by a court-appointed receiver. The receiver took control of Chancey's business and propoerty pending final court disposition of the CFTC suit.

The agency previously posted his photograph on the site and visitors can report any sighting by completing a form on the Web pages assigned to the case and E-mailing it to the CFTC enforcement division, the agency said.
